title: Karayakupovo Horizon
fact_summary: A name proposed in 2025 for the burial traditions of the southern Urals between about 750 and 1000, which archaeologists connect with the early Hungarians.

claims.text: A 2025 study writes: “We hereafter introduce the term ‘Karayakupovo Horizon’ (KH) to cover the diversity of the burial traditions and artefactual assemblages of the Southern Urals, including the Cis- and Trans-Urals, dated to 750–1000 CE and associated with putative Early Medieval Magyars”.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: The study names Uyelgi, near Chelyabinsk, as a reference cemetery of this horizon east of the Urals, and Bolshie Tigany in Tatarstan as “a key site” on the European side.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: It says the people of this horizon “lived in a multilingual and multiethnic context in the Circum-Uralic region, surrounded by Turkic, Finno-Permic, and Ugric-speaking people”.
claims.certainty_reason: The study's summary of the background, not its own finding; the works it cites have not been opened.

claims.text: An earlier study used the name differently, describing Bolshie Tigani and Tankeevka as Kushnarenkovo/Karayakupovo culture mixed with early Bulgars.
claims.certainty_reason: Read in the study when the Kushnarenkovo page was written; it shows the older use of the name as an archaeological culture.

claims.text: The ancestry best seen among these people and later found among the 10th-century Hungarians should be called “Karayakupovo-type”; the evidence “supports the hypothesis of a Trans-Uralian origin” for it.
claims.certainty_reason: A name and a reading proposed in one tier B study.

open_questions.text: The name groups cemeteries by their date and region. Did the people buried in them see themselves as one people?
How does the new name relate to the older terms Kushnarenkovo culture and Karayakupovo culture? The archaeological works behind them have not been opened.

review.note: Checked by Claude against open copies of every source. Marc spot-checks a sample.
